topic: CodeGraph for Claude Code and Cursor Guide 2026

key_points: Canonical project source positions CodeGraph as a local-first, pre-indexed code knowledge graph for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Gemini, Antigravity, Kiro, and Hermes Agent.
The documented workflow is install once with `codegraph install`, restart the agent, then run `codegraph init` per project so the agent can query the local `.codegraph/` index.
The README explains the core architecture: tree-sitter extraction, local SQLite storage with FTS5, reference resolution for calls/imports/inheritance, and native file-watcher auto-sync.
Strong source for exact commands, supported clients, CLI reference, troubleshooting, and claims that the index is derived deterministically from source rather than LLM summaries.
Direct SERP competitor with the same primary keyword and a complete-guide framing for Claude Code and Cursor users.
Covers install, MCP registration, initialization, FAQ, local execution, auto-sync behavior, and a caveat that published cost reductions are median benchmark results rather than guarantees.
SERP gap: the article includes an off-topic document-to-PPT section, so a cleaner guide can stay focused on AI coding workflows, measurement, and operational adoption.
Narrative competitor frames the problem as AI coding assistants wasting time rebuilding repository context with grep, glob, file reads, and exploratory searches.
Explains CodeGraph in accessible language: a local graph of symbols, relationships, call graphs, files, routes, and dependencies for tools including Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, and OpenCode.
Useful for reader pain language, but light on concrete Claude Code and Cursor setup details, governance, and how to prove ROI on a real team.
Performance-led competitor cites published benchmark-style claims: median 70% fewer tool calls, 59% lower token consumption, and 49% faster response time across author-tested repositories.
Strong hook for Claude Code users: one local graph query can answer architectural questions that normally require multiple reads and searches.
SERP gap: emphasizes headline savings more than reproducible team evaluation, staleness handling, security review, or Cursor-specific configuration.
Practical guide positions CodeGraph as a local map for Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, OpenCode, Hermes Agent, and similar tools.
Covers pain points such as repeated grep/find/Read calls, unclear callers/callees before edits, route-handler discovery, and architecture questions burning tokens.
Includes useful caution that CodeGraph reduces exploration overhead but does not replace normal code review or tests.
Strategic competitor frames local code graphs as an agent context layer, not just a Claude Code helper.
Highlights an adoption path: start with one large repo and one narrow workflow such as routing changes, SDK API changes, refactors, test-target selection, onboarding, or impact analysis.
Useful differentiation angle: measure tool calls before first edit, file reads before first edit, wrong-file edits, missed-impact review comments, staleness incidents, and verification quality.
Directory-style competitor summarizes CodeGraph as an MCP server that maps files, functions, classes, Terraform resources, and Markdown documentation into a Kuzu/SQLite-backed graph and FTS index.
Lists feature surfaces readers may search for: symbol lookup, call graph analysis, documentation outlining, graph visualization, status/logs/call history, and agent integration.
SERP gap: useful feature list, but lacks workflow guidance for Claude Code versus Cursor and lacks adoption trade-offs.

stats.fact: As of July 3, 2026, the GitHub repository `colbymchenry/codegraph` had 57,231 stars, 3,523 forks, 269 open issues, and an MIT license.
The GitHub repository was created on January 18, 2026 and was last pushed on July 3, 2026, indicating active development at research time.
The latest npm package for `@colbymchenry/codegraph` was version 1.2.0 at research time, with platform packages for macOS, Linux, and Windows on x64 and arm64.
The CodeGraph README says the installer auto-detects and configures Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, opencode, Hermes Agent, Gemini CLI, Antigravity IDE, and Kiro.
The documented setup sequence is `codegraph install`, restart the agent, then run `codegraph init` inside each project to build the project graph.
CodeGraph stores project data in a local `.codegraph/codegraph.db` SQLite database with FTS5 full-text search.
The README says extraction uses tree-sitter AST parsing to identify functions, classes, methods, calls, imports, extends, and implements relationships.
The README says the MCP server watches project files, debounces changes with a 2-second quiet window, filters to source files, and incrementally syncs the graph.
The README says the default MCP guidance tells agents to reach for `codegraph_explore` for architecture, flow, and impact questions, and to check the staleness banner after edits.
The Tosea guide says CodeGraph uses MCP and works with Claude Code v2.x and current Cursor versions, while advising older Claude Code users to check release compatibility notes.
The Tosea guide says the ~35% cost reduction claim is a median across seven benchmark repositories and is not guaranteed on every codebase.
The Level Up Coding competitor reports headline benchmark claims of 70% fewer tool calls, 59% lower token use, and 49% faster response time, while tying the value to large-repo discovery tasks.

The Developers Digest competitor recommends judging local code graphs by tool calls before first edit, file reads before first edit, wrong-file edits, missed-impact review comments, staleness incidents, and verification quality.

angles: Write the guide as a practical Claude Code and Cursor setup playbook, not another hype piece about token savings.
Lead with the core problem: coding agents spend too much of their budget locating code before they can reason about changes.
Position CodeGraph as a local context layer for structural questions: callers, callees, routes, dependency paths, blast radius, and likely entry points.
Separate what CodeGraph can prove from what competitors imply: it can reduce repeated discovery work, but it does not guarantee universal cost savings or replace tests and review.
Include side-by-side Claude Code and Cursor configuration notes, with a short explanation of MCP registration and project initialization.
Make measurement a differentiator: show teams how to run the same task with and without CodeGraph and compare tool calls, file reads, first-edit time, wrong-file edits, and missed call sites.
Cover staleness and trust: explain auto-sync, manual `codegraph sync`, staleness banners, and when an agent should still inspect source directly.
Treat `.codegraph/` as operational infrastructure: discuss whether to commit it, ignore it, regenerate it in CI, or keep it developer-local.
Add governance for enterprise readers: local-only indexing is a plus, but agent config files, auto-allow permissions, and MCP servers still deserve supply-chain review.
Clarify when not to use it: small repos, throwaway prototypes, single-file fixes, unsupported language-heavy repos, or teams that cannot maintain agent configuration.
Use the CodeGraph story to explain the broader 2026 shift from raw context windows to indexed, queryable, repo-local agent context.
